data.name: SIN1 / MAPKAP1
data.description: Essential structural subunit of mTORC2 (stress-activated protein kinase-interacting protein 1). Required for mTORC2 assembly and integrity; controls the substrate specificity of mTORC2 toward Akt and other AGC kinases. Prolonged rapamycin treatment can disrupt SIN1-containing mTORC2 in some cell types but not others, which is one explanation for the impaired Akt signalling seen with chronic rapamycin.
data.description_beginner: A structural building block that mTORC2 (the second mTOR complex) needs in order to assemble and work properly. Long-term rapamycin use can eventually break apart mTORC2 that contains it, part of why chronic rapamycin can dull Akt signaling.

reading_levels.student: mTORC2 subunit whose PH domain makes the complex PI3K-responsive.
reading_levels.research: MAPKAP1. The PH domain inhibits mTORC2 until PIP3 relieves it – the cleanest mechanism for how growth factors reach mTORC2.

studies.authors: Facchinetti V; Ouyang W; Wei H; Soto N; Lazorchak A; Gould C; Lowry C; Newton AC; Mao Y; Miao RQ; Sessa WC; Qin J; Zhang P; Su B; Jacinto E

studies.model_system: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts lacking mTORC2 components (SIN1, rictor, mTOR) and human cell lines; yeast; mouse tissue; in vitro kinase assays
studies.finding: Cells lacking the mTORC2 components mTOR, SIN1 or rictor lost phosphorylation of Akt and of conventional protein kinase C at the turn motif, a site near the end of the kinase domain. This phosphorylation did not depend on growth factors, and the authors reported the same function in yeast. Turn-motif phosphorylation helped newly made Akt and PKC fold correctly and stay stable; without it, Akt was held by the chaperone Hsp90 and protected from ubiquitin-mediated breakdown. mTORC2 controlled the Akt turn-motif and hydrophobic-motif (Ser473) sites independently in vivo and phosphorylated both directly in vitro. Boundary: Cell culture, yeast and in vitro kinase assays, with mouse tissue for the in vivo site analysis. Shows a protein-maturation role of mTORC2, not an organismal phenotype. Drafted from the abstract only.

relations.mechanism: SIN1 holds the complex together and positions the substrate; without it mTORC2 cannot phosphorylate Akt.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SIN1 holds mTORC2 together and positions its target – without it, mTORC2 can't switch Akt on.
relations.boundary: Mammalian cell studies and a cryo-EM structure (JAC2006, FRI2006, YAN2006, STU2018). Cell and structural evidence; not tested in people by these sources.
